interface.title: Veridalis
interface.field: Ecology / biodiversity monitoring (field surveys, GBIF occurrence data)
interface.stage_of_work: Data cleaning, first-pass analysis, and screening/reporting after fieldwork
interface.what_it_is_for: Load a species survey or GBIF occurrence CSV, check its quality, compute diversity indices for each site and for the whole survey, map the sites by diversity class, flag sites that fall below your own thresholds, and export a text screening report.

data.note: Most of the survey used the built-in synthetic demo: 5 London sites, 25 records, 812 individuals. I also uploaded both test files. qc_test_survey.csv: 12 raw records, 5 flagged, 7 clean, 58.33% usability, 3 sites. gbif_test.csv.txt: 92 raw, 1 flagged, 91 clean, 98.91% usability; it collapsed to 1 site and 1 species with H'=0, but its report counted only 3 survey records and N=4. In the QC file, a 999999 abundance outlier ('Mystery sp.') passed QC and drove landscape H' down to 0.001.

tree.general: Screen a species survey for data quality and low-diversity sites, and record the result
tree.specific: Use Veridalis to audit a survey CSV, compute Shannon/Simpson/Pielou indices for each site (Margalef is reported only once, for the whole survey, inside the report), map the sites, flag them against H' and richness thresholds, and download the screening report

Download CSV template gives the expected columns (site_id, site_name, latitude, longitude, species, abundance, taxon, habitat, date)

screens_never_reached: A list of the individual flagged or quarantined records with their reasons (missing coordinates, invalid lat/lon, zero coordinates, missing taxon). The QC audit shows only counts, and Species records shows only records that passed, all with quality_flag OK.
A site-level display of the Margalef index. It appears only as one landscape value inside the report text, not in the metric cards or the table for each site.
Green (high) or amber (moderate) markers. No site in any of the three datasets reached those classes, so only red and dark red were seen.
not_done: I could not find out which specific records were flagged, or for what reason. The interface gives only the total flagged count and usability score.

I did not see the Darwin Core field mapping itself (how uploaded columns are matched to standard fields). For GBIF the Species records table keeps the raw GBIF columns (gbifid, license, rightsholder…), and the harmonized fields site_id, species and abundance are not clearly shown as a mapping. No task covers this because the interface never showed it.
The Download as CSV button on the Site biodiversity metrics toolbar was pressed but produced no downloaded file in this browser (a dead end, so it is not an action in the tree).
I did not press Send an Email (via Gmail). It opens an external mail.google.com link, which is outside the allowed host, and it is optional.
I did not try the Light and Dark basemaps or the Hide MiniMap link.

Behaviours to note, not fixed: (1) the Report preview goes stale after thresholds or the dataset change until Generate is pressed again; the old demo report stayed after uploading qc_test_survey.csv. (2) For qc_test_survey.csv the audit says 7 clean records but the report counts 6, and Species records shows 6 rows plus a blank row. (3) For the GBIF file the audit says 91 clean records but the report counts only 3 survey records and N=4, and Species records shows only 3 data rows followed by blank rows, so most records seem to be dropped before the metrics are computed. (4) The 999999 abundance outlier passed QC.
